name: Apteva Apps
description: Curated registry of Apteva Apps. Each entry points at a manifest URL the platform can fetch + install.

apps.name: llm
apps.description: Managed AI API access for Apteva-hosted apps and agents. OpenAI-compatible tenant-safe gateway with provider routing, bound provider integrations, provider model discovery, project and subject policy, token revocation, subject suspend/resume, idempotent usage tracking, spend caps, app-issued bearer tokens, and usage records for orchestration apps to consume.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: api
apps.description: Lightweight API gateway for Apteva SaaS projects. Owns public API hostnames, method/path routes, simple API keys, CORS policy, request logs, dashboard operations, and dispatch to Functions, installed app HTTP surfaces, or plain HTTP origins.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: saas
apps.description: Shared SaaS access control, checkout orchestration, no-card trials, and generic fulfillment for Apteva apps. Packages installed apps into sellable plans, creates or links Billing customers only when payment is required, creates Subscriptions and invoices, provisions Auth organizations and Entitlements, runs lifecycle actions against other apps such as Containers, stores live usage gauges from existing app tools, and applies subscription lifecycle state.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: stocks
apps.description: Explore + screen the S&P 1500 (every Dividend Aristocrat & King) backed by Yahoo Finance. Min/max filters on market cap, dividend yield, payout ratio, P/E, and 5-year dividend growth; smart watchlists (rule-driven, manual, or hybrid) with live membership; per-stock quote, price chart, dividend history. Read-only: never places orders, holds no ledger. Free Yahoo public endpoints, no API key.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: taxes
apps.description: Business tax profiles, VAT/IVA/TVA estimates, corporate and income tax estimates, social contribution obligations, filing status, payment tracking, and links to billing and bills for source data and outbound tax payments.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: simple
apps.description: Minimal read-only UI for watching an Apteva agent — embed anywhere on the same host. Same-origin, path-mounted SPA; no sidecar.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: demo
apps.description: Client-facing demo runner. State board with live MCP-polled scenario cards, control rail with seed/reset recipes + scripted scenario triggers, chat dock for natural-language Q&A with the agent. Designed as a kiosk surface for client meetings.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: tasks
apps.description: Mission board for an Apteva agent. Agents create and complete tasks via MCP tools; the dashboard tracks progress live. Tasks can be created in 'planning' mode for the agent to draft a proposal first.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: fetch
apps.description: Controlled HTTP client for agents and operators. Agents get one fetch_request MCP tool with bounded requests, hardened redirects, SSRF protection, encrypted secrets, and redacted history. The responsive dashboard panel provides an API editor, saved requests, environments, and paginated execution history.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: todo
apps.description: Personal todo list — human-first counterpart to the agent mission board. Inbox / Today / Upcoming, lists (user-facing buckets), tags (cross-cutting context), priorities, due dates, snooze, and recurrence. Agent helps via natural-language quick-add, list, snooze, and complete tools.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: notes
apps.description: Simple searchable notes for Apteva agents and human teams. Capture customer ideas, meeting notes, research snippets, decisions, and follow-ups with lightweight kinds, tags, source metadata, and a practical project page.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: voice-notes
apps.description: Lightweight audio notes for Apteva projects. Record voice memos from the browser, store the raw audio in Storage, and optionally transcribe through a bound Deepgram connection. Standalone by default so simple recording does not require CRM, Tasks, or meeting workflows.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: books
apps.description: Structured long-form manuscript workspace. Create books, organize chapters and sections, write in markdown, keep notes, track revisions, and export manuscripts.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: events
apps.description: Create shows, collect performer applications, curate lineups, issue simple tickets, and run check-in. Built for small events and comedy-style performer intake: applications can be shortlisted, accepted, rejected, then scheduled into performance slots. Free/manual ticketing in v0.1; paid checkout can be delegated to an external URL.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: health
apps.description: Personal health log — weight, sleep, mood, heart rate, blood pressure, workouts. One flexible time-series table for any numeric metric plus a workouts list. Agent ingests natural-language one-liners ('weight 78.4', 'ran 5k 26min', 'bp 122/78') via health_log; the panel charts pinned kinds and lists recent sessions. v0.2 will add device sync (Apple Health, Oura, Garmin).
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: pantry
apps.description: Food inventory for pantry, fridge, and freezer. Track products, barcode aliases, locations, quantities, expiry batches, low-stock thresholds, and shopping-list needs. Agents can add/use stock from natural-language lines or structured MCP tools, then answer questions like what expires this week and what should I buy.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: recipes
apps.description: Recipe library, nutrition estimates, meal planning, and pantry-aware shopping lists. Agents can create structured recipes, scale servings, estimate macros, plan meals, generate merged shopping lists, and suggest meals from available ingredients.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: status
apps.description: Per-agent status line. Agent writes 'what I'm on right now' via MCP; dashboard reads it live. Short-horizon counterpart to the long-lived directive. Includes a panel for operators to view, set, and clear the line, plus a /status skill teaching the cadence + tone protocol.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: channels
apps.description: Global agent-facing channel router with explicit channels, conversations, and messages tables; Dashboard Chat as a project channel, full-width panel, Inbox, ntfy.sh project channels, Telegram channels with webhook callbacks and inline buttons, optional inbound routing, generic app-bus events, and channel deletion from the panel.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: crm
apps.description: Contacts, messaging inbox, lists, segments, and sales opportunities for Apteva agents and human teams, with project isolation and typed attributes.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: computer
apps.description: Watch and steer browser sessions, with rendered DOM extraction and Set-of-Mark label clicking. v0.7.45 adds opt-in structured Set-of-Mark targets in screenshot responses via include_som=true while keeping default MCP payloads small.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: screenshots
apps.description: Capture browser screenshots from a URL, save them to storage, and browse them in a gallery. Built on the `computer` app for the browser session and `storage` for the bytes — this app owns no browser plumbing itself. Four MCP tools (capture / list / get / delete) plus a gallery panel and a chat-attachable screenshot-card the agent posts after a successful capture. Idempotency_key on capture deduplicates retries within a 10-minute window. v0.1 supports URL-driven capture only; attaching to a session the agent already opened lands when computer exposes session resume.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: web
apps.description: Browser-native web intelligence with Google-default search, extract, crawl, map, research, response caching, rendered DOM parsing, and smart query-matched snapshot crops using Computer browser regions. v0.1.14 dedupes near-identical nested smart snapshot regions with the same heading and very high visual overlap.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: storage
apps.description: File storage with virtual folders, signed URLs, dedup. Pluggable backend: local disk by default, S3-compatible (AWS / R2 / B2 / Wasabi / MinIO) when configured. On S3, presigned upload + download URLs let clients transfer bytes directly to the bucket — bytes never proxy through this container. v0.9.5 adds files_get_content for inline byte fetch via CallAppResult — fixes the multi-storage-install case where signed URLs route to the wrong instance.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: tables
apps.description: Typed-row database for Apteva agents and human teams. The row-shaped sibling to storage: define typed tables (text, number, bool, datetime, json, file_id), insert rows with strict validation, query with typed predicates, paginate. Read-only SELECT escape hatch with {table_name} placeholders for aggregations the named tools can't express. Project-scoped by default; opt-in global tables for shared lookup data.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: jobs
apps.description: Scheduled-job runner for one-time, interval, and cron work. Dispatches platform-authorized sibling app tools, external HTTP targets, or agent events with bounded concurrency, reclaimable leases, retries, idempotency keys, and retained run history.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: functions
apps.description: Lambda-style serverless functions in node or Go. Each function is an immutable, built version served by a pool of warm worker processes — the runtime boots once and serves invocations over a socketpair, no per-request spawn. Handlers reach other Apteva apps via context.call. Deploy-time build (npm install / go build), immutable versions with rollback, auto-routed HTTP at /fn/<name>, and optional public Function URLs at /url/<name>/<token>.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: workflows
apps.description: Deterministic, on-demand pipelines. A workflow is a YAML/JSON graph of typed steps (http, function, app, integration, emit, branch) with goto-style branching and per-step retry. Triggered by HTTP, manual invocation, or another app's events (the sidecar opens one multiplexed SSE subscription per (source, project) lane); integration steps reach any in-project connection (Pushover, Slack, Resend, ...) by id without operator pre-binding. Per-step audit log so every run is inspectable, retryable, replayable. Strict separation from agents: workflows never call LLMs — if a step needs judgment it sends an event to an agent and the workflow ends.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: code
apps.description: Repositories — named, framework-tagged code workspaces scoped under Apteva projects. First-class editing tools modelled on Claude Code: partial reads with line numbers, exact-match string edits with uniqueness checks, atomic multi-edit, repo-wide grep + glob, ZIP import for repository initialization or overlay updates, editor-style SVG source-tree icons, and native repo issues for bugs, feature requests, tasks, comments, and code links. v0.5.18 makes coding tools more agent-efficient with compact grep modes, smaller paged reads, file outlines/excerpts, and dry-run unified patch application for large edits. v0.5.17 unifies project navigation with a single top tab bar and renames the global code view to Repositories. v0.5.16 gives the project-wide Issues inbox the full panel width and makes issue titles the primary row text with repo metadata below. v0.5.15 adds a project-wide Issues inbox in the UI so operators can scan and create issues across all repositories without selecting a repo first. v0.5.14 adds project-wide issue search for agents, defaults the issue UI to all states, and batches field edits in the edit modal. v0.5.13 moves issue metadata editing into a modal and keeps the issue detail page focused on title, body, links, and comments. v0.5.12 simplifies the issue UI with quieter issue rows, fewer visible filters, and compact metadata chips in the detail sidebar. v0.5.11 separates issue lifecycle state from workflow status: state=open|closed, reason=completed|not_planned, and status for board workflow such as todo, in_progress, blocked, or done. v0.5.10 promotes Code and Issues to top-level repository tabs, with the file tree scoped to the Code tab like a GitHub-style repo view.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: simulator
apps.description: iOS and Android simulators on demand. Boot a device, build a repo's source into an APK/.app, install + launch on a headless emulator or Simulator, stream the screen to the browser, and relay touch + key input. Called by Apteva Code on Run for mobile repos; usable standalone for any flow that produces a mobile artifact. v0.1.23 reconnects live view after transient proxy or sidecar interruptions instead of leaving the panel permanently on Stream closed.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: media
apps.description: Catalog + derivations + renders + transcripts + auto-descriptions for audio/video/image files in storage. Pluggable render backend: ffmpeg by default, Cloudinary when bound (offload trim/resize/transcode/crop/extract_frame). Subscribes to storage events for instant indexing on upload + cascade cleanup on delete; falls back to a 30s safety-net poll. Smart video thumbnails skip black/fade openings.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: podcast
apps.description: Podcast hosting and RSS feed management for Apteva projects. Create shows and episodes, attach Storage-hosted audio, probe durations through Media, publish valid RSS/iTunes XML feeds, track downloads, and expose custom feed domains through platform ingress with optional DNS writes via the Domains app.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: embed
apps.description: Create shareable viewer links and oEmbed-compatible responses for storage-backed files and media. Embed keeps publishing concerns out of storage: storage owns bytes and signed URLs; media can enrich thumbnails and dimensions; Embed owns the public viewer, iframe HTML, and oEmbed JSON.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: media-downloader
apps.description: yt-dlp-backed media download sidecar for Apteva. Probes supported media URLs, runs async video or audio downloads, uploads completed files into Storage, and supports private, age-restricted, or member-only downloads through encrypted YouTube and Patreon Netscape cookie source profiles. v0.2.9 adds configurable extra yt-dlp arguments so installs can enable JavaScript challenge solving, e.g. --js-runtimes node:/path/to/node for current YouTube media 403 cases.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: media-studio
apps.description: Generate or edit images, video, audio, music, and talking-head avatar videos via compatible providers. v0.10.43 fixes model-specific image options under multiple provider bindings, stale responses after tab switches, required image-to-video references in the UI and Venice backend, project-scoped Storage previews, upload MIME and size validation, per-kind durations, local-cache details, and responsive/accessibility behavior. v0.10.42 fixes project-scoped panel writes by including project_id in generation and avatar-creation proxy URLs, preventing immediate 404 responses before provider execution. v0.10.41 rebuilds the panel with React's production JSX runtime and adds a regression test that rejects development-only jsxDEV artifacts. v0.10.40 supports multiple bound audio providers, adds Fish Audio TTS and voice catalogs, and makes voice cloning provider-neutral across Fish Audio and ElevenLabs from uploaded audio, Storage references, URLs, data URLs, or base64. The UI exposes provider selection, generic voice cloning, Fish output format, and prosody speed. media_models exposes merged provider-prefixed image and audio model ids when multiple providers are bound. v0.10.39 filters unsupported ElevenLabs request-stitching fields for Eleven v3 and zero-retention requests while preserving text continuity where supported, and forwards current language-normalization voice options. v0.10.38 makes image output_format the final stored-file contract: JPEG requests convert mismatched PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF provider bytes before Storage and flatten transparency onto white; PNG requests are also re-encoded when needed, while mismatched WebP fails instead of storing mislabeled bytes. media_generate supports image / video / audio_tts / audio_sfx / music / avatar; media_estimate estimates generation cost; media_delete removes generations and linked files. Async video/avatar jobs queue and poll automatically. Optionally saves outputs to Storage.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: persona-studio
apps.description: Virtual influencer and reusable persona workspace. Owns consistent identities, style profiles, Storage-backed references, reusable items/products/props/locations, campaigns, generated assets, cache keys, and Composer handoffs while Media Studio remains the provider-neutral generator. v0.1.19 sends persona and item visual references as source_images for image, video, and avatar generation, including persona-owned Composer composition AI clips.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: composer
apps.description: Multi-clip video and audio composition. Stitch generated or uploaded assets into a single video with layered visual tracks, timed audio tracks, optional soundtrack, storage-aware render saves, overlay/text tracks, and AI-generated sources. v0.5.8 preserves planned fit_generated_keep_start avatar/video slots while recording actual generated duration separately, and renders gapped, overlapping, or out-of-order base clips on an absolute timeline so later PIP layers remain synchronized. Contiguous and legacy implicit base tracks retain the efficient concat path. v0.5.7 hardens ElevenLabs narration with timeline-ordered continuity across silence and SFX, stable text-based cache identity, persisted provider request IDs, immediate-text fallback, shared panel/render generation, conservative partial-setting defaults, and generated-TTS loudness normalization. Public installs use the stable V1 timeline/render surface while experimental Composer V2 remains gated for internal development.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: calendar
apps.description: Self-contained calendar — multiple calendars per project, events with recurrence (rrule), holidays helper. Agents read + write via MCP tools; the panel renders day / week / month / year / agenda views with click-to-create and drag-to-move. Multi-day + all-day events render clearly across views: truly continuous spanning bars in month view (per-week overlay), a dedicated all-day strip above the week/day timed grid, and connected span bars in the larger year mini-calendars.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: bookings
apps.description: Calendly-style booking links for human and AI-agent meetings. Booking types define availability, duration, intake fields, routing target, and meeting location. Bookings reads free slots from Calendar, creates the booked Calendar event, optionally creates a Calls room, and can attach invitees and booking activity to CRM.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: trips
apps.description: Plan trips end-to-end: destinations, transport, accommodation, activities, packing list, budget. Calendar sync keeps scheduled trip, transport, stay, and activity events in step. Trip ideas can hold candidate destinations, stays, transport, and activities before dates are known; adding dates schedules them. Optional Duffel and Google Places integrations power search, global deal scans, airport autocomplete, and route/date heatmaps.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: social
apps.description: Schedule and publish posts to your social media accounts (X, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Pinterest, Threads). Connect accounts from inside the app — no separate integration setup. Posts can be triggered from the panel or by an agent via MCP tools.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: commons
apps.description: User-owned public social node for the open web. Commons hosts local profiles, posts, follows, blocks, ActivityPub/WebFinger endpoints, signed outbound federation delivery, server-native ingress exposure for public hostnames, and a dashboard panel for operating a federated identity from an Apteva-controlled domain.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: messaging
apps.description: Send and receive messages across channels (email via SES, SMS+WhatsApp via Twilio). Tracks SES/SNS delivery events including delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complaints, delays, rejects, and rendering failures; mirrors them into Apteva message events and the operator panel. Sender setup can be rechecked idempotently to refresh SES identity, DNS, inbound receiving, SNS notifications, and delivery event wiring.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: campaigns
apps.description: Bulk-send orchestrator for CRM audiences. Compose email, SMS, or WhatsApp campaigns against CRM lists or segments, materialize recipients, schedule batch sends through Jobs, deliver via Messaging, respect suppression, add email unsubscribe links, and track per-recipient campaign status.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: whatsapp-web
apps.description: Linked-device WhatsApp provider for WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business app accounts. Pair with a QR code, send and receive text messages through WhatsApp Web, and expose provider-shaped tools for Messaging integration. This is not the official WhatsApp Business Platform API.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: email-checker
apps.description: Stateless email validation — no DB, every call resolves fresh. email_check returns RFC 5322 syntax, DNS MX records, and list-based classification (disposable provider, free provider, role account) with a combined valid verdict. email_check_smtp runs an EHLO + MAIL FROM <> + RCPT TO probe against the domain's MX, flagging informative=false for Google/Microsoft (which accept every RCPT) and for blocked or greylisted responses. Also exposes a REST mirror at /check?email=.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: domains
apps.description: DNS + domain inventory and registrar workflows for Apteva projects. v0.5 adds exact record-ID edits and deletes, safe multi-record RRset handling, project-isolated connections, strict provider errors and Spaceship pagination, serialized DNS mutations, and expiring idempotent confirmation intents for paid registration.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: deploy
apps.description: Local-first builds and runtime supervision for Apteva projects. Pluggable source kinds (code, local) and frameworks (go, static, blank) — fetches source, runs the framework toolchain, supervises the result as a child process bound to a local port. Code-app deployments stream repository exports over HTTP instead of base64 MCP payloads, boot recovery restarts orphaned live releases from their saved build, and custom domains now register through server-native ingress/cert management instead of requiring the Routes or Certs apps.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: channel-chat
apps.description: Chat bridge between the agent and the dashboard / external channels. Persists messages with monotonic ids for clean reconnect. Currently bundled with apteva-server as a built-in framework app; will be extracted to a standalone installable app in a future release.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: trading
apps.description: Trading desk for Apteva agents. Multi-portfolio, multi-asset (equity, crypto, polymarket). Each portfolio runs in paper mode (deterministic in-process engine) or live mode (orders route through a bound broker integration; v0.2 ships Binance only). Mandate, allowed asset classes, and daily-loss halt enforced server-side; halt cancels working broker orders upstream. Approval policy lives in the agent's directive, not the platform.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: torrent
apps.description: BitTorrent client + indexer-search frontend. Search across configured Jackett / Prowlarr / RSS sources, add downloads by magnet or .torrent URL; on completion the resulting files are uploaded to the storage app and probed by media. Generic — ships with no indexers preconfigured; the user supplies sources and is responsible for what they download.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: dlna
apps.description: Publishes a UPnP/DLNA MediaServer on the LAN. Smart TVs, game consoles, Sonos, VLC, and other AV clients discover the server via SSDP and browse a virtual library backed by the storage app for bytes + folder structure, and the media app for duration / codec / resolution metadata. No transcoding in v0.1: clients that can't decode the source codec see the file in the listing but won't play it.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: backup
apps.description: Backup engine for Apteva platform snapshots and app-provided scoped backups. Platform runs capture the server DB plus running sidecar app DBs through /api/platform/snapshot; app-scoped runs let providers such as Fleet hand Backup a per-resource snapshot for destination upload, scheduling, retention, history, and restore. Destinations support local disk and S3-compatible buckets (AWS, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO). Schedules are driven by the Jobs app.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: live-link
apps.description: Public HTTPS URL for a locally-installed Apteva instance. Two modes: quick (default) spawns a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel for an anonymous trycloudflare.com URL on every start — zero config, no account; named uses a Cloudflare API token + account/zone IDs to give a stable URL on a hostname you own (e.g. tunnel.example.com), creating-or-adopting a cfd_tunnel, configuring its ingress via the API, and upserting a proxied CNAME — restarts reuse the same URL. Surfaces in the project page with copy/stop/destroy controls and a runs history tagged by mode. Four MCP tools (expose_start/stop/status/destroy) let agents drive both modes. Auto-installs cloudflared on first use for linux/{amd64,arm64,arm,386} and darwin/{amd64,arm64}; falls back to PATH or a config-pinned binary on other hosts. ngrok, tailscale-funnel, and PUBLIC_URL auto-rewrite arrive in v0.3+.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: billing
apps.description: Customers, invoices, payments, refunds, reusable payment methods, and PDF/HTML invoice rendering. v0.8.17 partitions issuer legal and bank identity by project, reconciles Stripe Checkout against persisted session amount and currency, charges the exact outstanding balance including tax and fractional-quantity lines, retries failed webhook processing, limits public webhook bodies, records multiple partial refunds idempotently, reopens refunded paid invoices, rounds tax correctly, and requires a patched Go toolchain. Catalog price snapshots and generic prepared invoice lines remain product-agnostic.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: catalog
apps.description: Products and prices — the source-of-truth app for what your business sells. Modelled after Stripe's Product + Price split: one product, many prices (different currencies, intervals, tiers). Lower-layer commerce app — catalog calls nothing; downstream apps call here. Prices are effectively immutable for financial fields after create (unit_amount_cents, currency, interval, metering fields) — to change pricing, create a new price and archive the old one. v0.1.2 adds generic metered price metadata (billing_scheme, meter_key, unit_label, unit_size) for orchestrators such as Hosting to sell included usage plus overage while Catalog remains provider-neutral. Soft-delete only so invoice/subscription references always resolve. Two-column panel with list + detail and form modals. Chat-attachable product-card and price-card components.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: inventory
apps.description: Reusable stock ledger for Apteva apps. Tracks SKUs, stock locations, on-hand quantities, reservations, transfers, adjustments, receipts, and an append-only movement audit trail. Commerce, Orders, Subscriptions, and fulfillment apps can reserve and commit stock without owning inventory logic themselves. Catalog links are optional, so inventory works for standalone SKUs as well as sellable products.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: entitlements
apps.description: Shared access-control and usage layer. Grants, revokes, checks, and meters access for SaaS plans, courses, memberships, digital downloads, paid content, manual grants, trials, promos, and usage quotas.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: orders
apps.description: Generic commerce fulfillment ledger for physical, hosting, SaaS, digital, and service products. Orders records durable paid/unpaid order state, line items, customer snapshots, fulfillment submissions, external fulfillment refs, retries/errors, shipment tracking, returns, and an append-only event log. v0.2.1 fixes Billing invoice lookup for orders_create_from_invoice while keeping the v0.2 generic order_type and fulfillment_app/fulfillment_type support.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: subscriptions
apps.description: Generic recurring-commerce lifecycle for SaaS, physical product subscriptions, memberships, and services. Owns recurrence, subscription status, current periods, renewal cycles, and references to invoice, order, or entitlement outputs. v0.2.0 adds generic flat and metered subscription items, idempotent usage records, period usage summaries, prepared invoice lines, and subscription invoice creation through Billing. Emits specific lifecycle events such as subscription.active, subscription.past_due, subscription.paused, subscription.ended, subscription.item.created, subscription.usage.recorded, and subscription.invoice.requested.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: checkout
apps.description: Cart + buy flow — the orchestrator that turns a customer's intent into a real billing invoice. Three tables (carts, cart_items, checkout_sessions) implement the full state machine: open → checkout (locked while a session is awaiting payment) → converted (terminal, linked to billing invoice) or abandoned (TTL). Sits between content (storefront rendering) and billing (order ledger). Cart items snapshot from catalog prices at add-time so totals stay stable even if catalog pricing changes mid-session. On pay, calls billing.customers_upsert_by_email + invoices_create + invoices_finalize to mint a real invoice (idempotent + auditable). v0.1.2 adds cart_create so upstream apps such as Commerce can create or reuse carts by session token. v0.2.0 adds Stripe Checkout Session via the same payment_processor integration billing uses, with webhook-driven auto-paid flow. 10 MCP tools across cart_* and checkout_*. Admin panel with Carts + Sessions tabs.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: commerce
apps.description: Shopify-style multi-store commerce layer for Apteva. Owns stores, storefront listings, variants, collections, carts, checkout orchestration, and sales while delegating product/price truth to Catalog, cart/payment flow to Checkout, stock to Inventory, invoices to Billing, and fulfillment records to Orders.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: creators
apps.description: Patreon-like memberships for creators and communities. Manage tiers, members, gated posts, protected file drops, billing payment links, optional CRM contact sync, and member announcements through Messaging. Storage holds gated files; Billing owns customers/invoices/payments; Creators owns entitlements and the member portal.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: community
apps.description: Circle/Skool-shaped community platform. Multiple communities per install, each with spaces (feed/forum/chat/course), member directory, posts and reactions, in-app DMs, and courses with sections, lessons, comments, and progress. Panel updates live via the platform event bus. Storage and ffmpeg bindings are optional for lesson videos and duration probing.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: bills
apps.description: Vendors, bills, and outbound payments — the AP mirror of billing. Lifecycle (received → approved → scheduled → paid) plus disputed / void. Per-bill provider field stays local in v0.1.x; bank-rail providers (Mercury / Wise / Bill.com) land in v0.2. PDF voucher rendering for filing/audit. Drop a PDF on the bills tab and it's uploaded straight away — bind OpenCode Go (Kimi K2.6 default, vision-capable) in the Bindings tab and OCR auto-fills vendor + line items + dates + totals automatically (binding IS the on switch as of v0.1.5; no separate config flip required). Caller args always win. PDF rendering via embedded PDFium-WASM (no CGO, no system deps). Storage app is a declared dep so it auto-installs.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: finance
apps.description: Unified personal-wealth tracker — cash, brokerage positions, P2P loans, crypto, real estate, vehicles, pensions, loans, all in one ledger. Three nouns model everything: accounts (a place that holds value), instruments (the thing held — AAPL, BTC, EUR, your house), holdings (account × instrument → quantity + cost basis). Money in signed integer minor units; avg-cost accounting with cost_basis_delta on every txn so realised P&L is one column sum. Convenience tools for buy/sell/dividend/interest/transfer/valuation. Reports: net worth (point or monthly series, by account/kind/currency), allocation, performance (realised + unrealised P&L), cashflow (income vs expense per period). Per-category monthly budgets with hierarchical rollup. CSV import. v0.1 is manual entry; v0.2 plugs in integrations (Trading 212 first, then Plaid / Mintos / Binance) via the platform integrations engine — manual and integrated rows are indistinguishable downstream.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: mqtt
apps.description: Embedded MQTT broker for Apteva. Acts as the LAN message bus for smart-home devices (ESP32, Zigbee2MQTT, Tasmota, anything that speaks MQTT 3.1.1 or 5.0). Every published message is mirrored onto the platform event bus as `mqtt.message` so sibling apps (messaging, jobs, calendar) can react without speaking MQTT themselves; per-pattern subscriptions promote interesting topics to named bus events. Auto-discovers Home Assistant-convention devices by parsing `homeassistant/+/+/config`. Username/password auth + per-user topic ACL; an `apteva-default` user is seeded with a random password on first install (logged once).
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: tapo
apps.description: Local-LAN control of TP-Link Tapo cameras. Pan/tilt/zoom, snapshots, browser live view, RTSP stream URLs, app-level camera pause, ONVIF motion/person events surfaced in the camera UI, privacy + LED + night-mode toggles, presets. Talks the camera's secure_passthrough and ONVIF interfaces directly with no cloud round-trips. Setup requires enabling Third-Party Compatibility in the Tapo app and using the dedicated Camera Account credentials.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: ffmpeg
apps.description: Stateless ffmpeg-as-a-service for sibling Apteva apps. Three sync MCP tools — ffmpeg_grab_frame, ffmpeg_probe, ffmpeg_version — that wrap the local ffmpeg/ffprobe binaries. tapo's snapshot_capture is the v0.1 use case: grab one frame from a camera's RTSP stream without forcing every camera-y app to bundle its own ffmpeg. No DB, no panel, no async tools — minimal shape. Requires ffmpeg + ffprobe on PATH; OnMount refuses to start with a clear 'install ffmpeg' error if either is missing.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: docs
apps.description: Generate client-facing PDFs from markdown templates and store them in storage. Pure-Go render pipeline (no Chromium): markdown body + Go-template placeholders, rendered via maroto. Audit trail on every render — who rendered what template with which data — for compliance use cases (invoices, contracts, NDAs). Past renders keep working even after a template is edited because the output is a stable storage file_id.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: instances
apps.description: Compute-host inventory + lifecycle for Apteva. Manages the local Apteva machine and remote VPS instances under one MCP/REST surface so other apps (Live Link self-vps, Deploy SSHRuntime, Backup off-host, future Containers/Database/MQTT/game-server apps) bind a single "compute" dependency instead of each speaking VPS-provider APIs directly. The local machine is auto-seeded as instance id=0 and is always 'ready' — cannot be created or destroyed via the public API. Remote instances are provisioned via Hetzner Cloud. Per-instance Ed25519 SSH keypair seeded into the box via cloud-init authorized_keys; background readiness probe flips status='provisioning' → 'ready' once SSH accepts the key. MCP tools cover create/get/list/destroy/run/upload/download/wait/metrics so higher-level apps can transfer artifacts between local and remote hosts. Vitals (CPU / mem / disk / net / load / uptime) via gopsutil locally and a /proc-parsing bash script over SSH remotely, cached 5s per host.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: compute
apps.description: Shared transient compute queue for Apteva apps. Apps submit short-lived resource-heavy jobs, and Compute serializes them across local or remote hosts with priority, ownership, timeout, cancellation, and run history. It is the resource scheduler layer between high-level apps such as Media/Composer and low-level host providers such as Instances.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: containers
apps.description: Generic Docker workload runtime for Apteva. Runs arbitrary container images on local or remote Instances hosts with pull policies, bounded pre-start file and secret injection, named volumes, ports, health checks, logs, lifecycle actions, storage usage metrics, and built-in blueprints. v0.1.26 fixes blueprint pull and host overrides, preserves reused volumes during failed starts, redacts stored environment values, adds ownership-aware cleanup and payload limits, removes mutable root installer scripts, improves health and list performance, and adds a complete responsive deployment form.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: hosting
apps.description: Managed container-backed hosting control plane for Apteva tenants, arbitrary Docker images, and starter WordPress hosting products. Hosting provisions containers, exposes default hostnames through platform ingress, tracks generic runtime usage for plan enforcement, orchestrates Catalog, Billing, Subscriptions, Orders, and Entitlements for paid/free hosting sale flows, and can optionally provision Auth org/user/client records for hosted admin panels. v1.10.0 keeps Hosting as the product orchestrator while wiring tenant add-ons into generic Subscriptions items/usage, optional LLM subject/token orchestration, llm.usage.recorded ingestion, included-usage tracking, and subscription-backed metered overage invoicing.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: fleet
apps.description: Control plane for a fleet of client Apteva instances. Spawns each tenant with its own data dir and port, supervised by Fleet; hosted tenants can run on the parent server or on VPS instances. Includes tenant_clone and tenant_migrate for local/remote host-to-host transfer, read-only cloning with consistent SQLite snapshots, cold moves with rollback, streamed local-to-hosted transfers for large full clones, provider hooks for Backup, admin-driven bootstrap, encrypted api_key keyring, server-native ingress/cert registration for tenant hostnames, delegated DNS/domain grants, generic provider grants for sharing parent integrations into tenants, generic tenant inventory/platform/app-MCP control tools, health polling, boot reconciliation, tenant updates, and support-login tools.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: robot
apps.description: Agent navigation eval sandbox. 2D grid worlds the agent perceives partially (radius=2 default) and moves through one cardinal cell at a time. Episodes terminate via the harness — success on goal-reach or timeout at max_steps; the agent has no quit tool. A* baseline computed at scenario load powers an optimality_ratio metric on every successful run. Five gameplay tools (observe / move / pick / drop / no-give-up) plus three control tools (list_scenarios / start_episode / episode_status). pick + drop are reserved in the contract for v0.2 items. Three starter scenarios: empty_room, corridor (S-shape), warehouse_01 (three shelves).
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: vpn
apps.description: Backend-agnostic VPN orchestrator. Provisions a VPN server on an Instances host (local id 0 or a Hetzner VPS), generates keys, uploads daemon config, brings the interface up, and polls peer statistics on a timer. v0.1 ships WireGuard with native client support on macOS, iOS, Windows, Android, and Linux — the .conf returned by vpn_peer_add imports unchanged into every platform's official WG app. The internal Backend interface accommodates OpenVPN / IKEv2 later without changes to the MCP tool surface; tool names are protocol-neutral (vpn_peer_add, not wg_peer_add). Peers are created and revoked exclusively via MCP tools; the panel is monitor-only.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: certs
apps.description: TLS certificate issuance for Apteva projects via Let's Encrypt (or any RFC 8555 ACME directory). Two challenge types: DNS-01 routes TXT writes through the Domains app (no registrar credentials held here); HTTP-01 uses the webroot pattern (writes /.well-known/acme-challenge/<token> to a directory served by whatever reverse proxy is on :80 — Caddy, nginx, traefik). cert_issue accepts a per-request challenge_type override and remembers it for renewal. Async issuance, daily renewal worker, privileged cert_material tool gated to the server's TLS cache.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: routes
apps.description: Hostname-based routing for Apteva — owns the table mapping public hostnames (blog.example.com) to local backend targets (http://127.0.0.1:7100). Apps register routes via routes_register; apteva-server reads the table and reverse-proxies inbound traffic. Optional: uninstall and the platform falls back to path-based routing. Works the same for cloud installs (browser → public IP → apteva-server) and tunnel installs (cloudflared etc).
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: cdn
apps.description: Public-facing edge for apps that emit URLs. Composes optional Domains-managed DNS with apteva-server native ingress/TLS into one capability: given an origin and a hostname, expose it publicly. Passive zones route directly to an origin URL or installed app. Active zones route traffic through CDN itself; for Storage, origin_auth=signed_url lets CDN serve private files on a public hostname by minting short Storage signed URLs server-side and streaming the bytes back. Consumers call cdn_url_for_app to mint URLs through CDN binding policy, while cdn_url_for remains available for explicit zone-id URL assembly. The deprecated Certs and Routes apps are no longer CDN dependencies.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: redirects
apps.description: Branded short links and domain redirects. Each rule maps a (hostname, path) pair to an external URL and answers with a 301/302/307/308 + Location header. Think Bitly on your own domain, or EasyRedir for post-rebrand migrations. Uses server-native ingress to claim public hostnames so apteva-server reverse-proxies inbound traffic here, with TLS handled by platform ingress. Optionally composes with Domains to upsert an A or CNAME record pointing at the platform when the apex is managed there. Match modes: exact and prefix (longest wins, segment-boundary safe); preserve_path forwards the leftover path on prefix rules, preserve_query merges inbound query strings.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: affiliate
apps.description: Publisher-side affiliate manager for offers, monetized links, and normalized performance across Target Circle/Circlewise, Impact, Awin, CJ Affiliate, Amazon Associates, Skimlinks, Sovrn, PartnerStack, and ShareASale. v0.1.7 adds complete provider pagination, correct cross-page aggregation and monetary rounding, link attribution, capability-aware syncs, safer credential handling, and a responsive paginated panel with date ranges and mixed-currency reporting.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: partner-program
apps.description: Merchant-side referral and affiliate program for SaaS, services, and commerce. Track approved partners, campaigns, referral links and codes, referred customers, and commission ledger entries. MVP uses five tables and manual payout tracking so teams can run a real program before adding payout automation.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: ads
apps.description: Paid advertising control plane for Apteva. Manage ad accounts, campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, and audiences behind one MCP surface. v0.1 supports Meta Ads (Facebook + Instagram) and Google Ads, with OAuth account connection and account picking handled at runtime.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: seo
apps.description: Locale-aware SEO research workbench for domains, keywords, rankings, backlinks, and cached provider metrics. Includes a dashboard panel for interactive seeding, DataForSEO location sync, human-triggered paid refreshes, a domain page-ranking drill-down, and daily ranking history in the existing rankings table. v0.3.7 fixes DataForSEO domain refresh payloads for the current Google domain_rank_overview API; MCP tools stay read/write for tracked entities and read-only for cached SEO data.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: content
apps.description: Multi-site block-based CMS. One project hosts 1..N sites — each with its own posts, pages, terms, menus, settings, theme, and optional hostname. Per-site templates (Finance Blog, SaaS Marketing, Docs Site bundled). Posts and pages with hierarchy, media, taxonomies, menus, revisions, redirects. Canonical body is a JSON block tree; 16 core block types shipped. Dashboard panel includes a Content tab (list + block editor), Templates tab (one-click site scaffolds), and a site switcher that auto-hides on single-site installs. Renders themed HTML at /, /posts/:slug, /:nested-page, term archives, feed.xml, and sitemap.xml; host-based dispatch routes domain-linked traffic to the right site automatically. Same data exposed as REST under /api/apps/content/admin/* so external frontends share the database without touching the theme path.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: gigs
apps.description: Agents delegate atomic work to human workers (CRM contacts) by composing reusable multi-modal instructions — text, audio, video, images, documents, checklists, confirmations, and the full input_* family. Templates are saved instruction sets; gigs are dispatched snapshots whose result schema, media manifest, and checklist are derived from the composition (never hand-authored). Workers receive a magic-link page via crm.contacts_send_message, read/watch the instructions, fill the form, upload attachments through storage, and submit. Yes/no and short-text gigs also accept thread replies via the CRM conversation. workers_create upserts a CRM contact and promotes it to a worker in one MCP call. CRM and storage are required dependencies; messaging is reached indirectly through CRM.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: auth
apps.description: Identity layer for Apteva-deployed SaaS: email + password signup/login, EdDSA JWT issuance with JWKS, refresh-token rotation, OAuth client registry, app-specific user metadata, email verification, password reset, magic links, and TOTP MFA. Agents administer organizations, users, clients, and metadata via MCP tools; the deployed frontend hits the public HTTP routes; the dashboard renders a consolidated Auth panel (Overview / Users / Clients / Endpoints). Messaging is an optional dependency for transactional email.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: market-intel
apps.description: Cross-source market-intelligence gateway for trading agents. Ask in domain language ("Alcaraz clay H2H", "current Fed-cut probability", "enrich this Polymarket market") and market-intel fans out to the right bound data sources — prediction markets, sportsbook odds, macro, news, crypto — normalizes, de-vigs, and returns one consistent result. Read-only: it reads prices/stats/history; the agent decides; the trading app executes. v0.1 ships the unified query gateway; the background signal engine (arbitrage detection + events) lands in v0.2.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: analytics
apps.description: Generic event analytics for Apteva apps. Three ingest paths: bus auto-capture, analytics_track, and static-site tag collection. analytics_query / count / top / topics / sum surface aggregates over JSON props. The dashboard panel is real-time, with Overview, Dashboards, Catalog, Tracking, and Capture tabs. v0.8 adds an event catalog / tracking plan: event specs, typed property specs, validation modes, violation reporting, and spec-driven auto upsert / rollup policies for imported daily metrics and live counters. v0.8.1 fixes Catalog loading under the SDK's single SQLite connection runtime. v0.8.2 lets dashboard stat and timeseries widgets sum numeric event fields, so aggregate observations such as Patreon daily post views can chart total views per day instead of observation row counts. v0.8.3 adds dashboard-level filters, dynamic filter option discovery, filter-aware widget evaluation, and a Patreon Overview template with Page, Currency, and Window controls. Dashboards persist project-scoped widget layouts for live page views, active sessions, top pages, devices, and recent activity.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: webinars
apps.description: Live, scheduled, multi-slot, and replay webinars. Owns registration pages, registrants, reminders, attendance, chat, polls, offers, replay publishing, and engagement reporting. v0.1.1 adds generic webinar slots so scheduled, multi-session, and evergreen-style webinars share one registration model.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: calls
apps.description: Standalone realtime audio/video calls with WebRTC-ready rooms, join tokens, unified human/agent/service participants, chat, transcripts, and app-bus lifecycle events. Agents join with the same participant primitives as humans; no dependency on streaming.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: telephony
apps.description: Voice calls via Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, SignalWire, or Vonage, with Twilio inbound routing for agent pickup. Outbound calls and answered inbound calls run as realtime sub-threads in core, with carrier audio bridged through a provider media stream. Includes MCP tools for placing, routing, answering, rejecting, hanging up, and listing calls, plus a dashboard panel for active and recent call operations.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: testimonials
apps.description: Lightweight customer proof store for Apteva with consent-aware publication, text and media testimonials, exact filtering, pagination, and a responsive management panel. V1 uses one testimonials table and declares Storage as an optional dependency only.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: environments
apps.description: Project-scoped isolated test environments built from installed app sidecars, selected or fake connections, deterministic MCP seed plans, runtime agents, virtualized edge traffic, assertions, and reusable snapshots. Provides a compact project panel plus MCP orchestration for eval apps and agents. v0.1.1 removes the desktop content-width cap so the project panel uses the available dashboard width.
apps.author: Apteva
